findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff imports org.keycloak.operator.crds.v2alpha1.deployment.spec.FeatureSpec and calls kc.getSpec().setFeatureSpec(new FeatureSpec()) / getFeatureSpec().getEnabledFeatures(), but the v2alpha1 KeycloakSpec in this branch exposes no featureSpec field — features are configured via spec.getUnsupported()/UnsupportedSpec, so the test file does not compile against the current CRD classes. The operator integration test module fails to compile ('cannot find symbol FeatureSpec' / 'method setFeatureSpec not found'), so the entire operator test suite cannot run and CI blocks the merge.

[BUG] The Dockerfile unconditionally appends --features=rolling-updates to kc.sh build, but this image script is (via the VERSION arg) also built against previously released Keycloak versions in upgrade tests, and the rolling-updates feature only exists in this new build — an older kc.sh rejects the unknown feature and the build step fails. Any test or workflow that uses Dockerfile-custom-image with VERSION pointing at a pre-rolling-updates release gets 'Unknown feature: rolling-updates' during docker build, breaking the upgrade-path scenarios this script exists to serve.

[ADVISORY] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently renumbered from 4 to 3 and 4 is repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED, changing the CLI contract for every existing consumer of 'kc update-compatibility check'. Any external automation, Operator version, or script written against the previously documented exit code 4 = 'recreate upgrade required' now interprets a recreate-required result (3) as success-adjacent and treats the new feature-disabled code (4) as recreate, producing wrong upgrade decisions during mixed-version operation; nothing in this diff audits in-tree consumers of the constant.

[ADVISORY] The feature-disabled branch calls picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) followed by return, relying on AbstractUpdatesCommand exposing an exit(int) exit mechanism whose behavior in this class hierarchy is unverified in the diff; if exit is inherited from a spec/command-line helper that throws, the subsequent statements are unreachable, and if it does not terminate the process the run() method continues to printPreviewWarning() only due to the explicit return — but the metadata command at UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java:46-50 duplicates the same pattern, so any mismatch in exit semantics breaks one but not the other. If picocli.exit does not map the code to the process exit status in this command context (e.g. it only sets an execution result consumed by the runner), scripts checking $? get an unexpected code and mis-classify a feature-disabled failure as a different error class.

[ADVISORY] testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message and never asserts the exit code equals CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4), leaving the new exit-code contract unverified even though the diff introduces it. A regression that makes the command exit with picocli's default usage/software error codes (1/2) or 0 instead of 4 passes the suite, silently breaking downstream consumers that branch on the feature-disabled exit code.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently changed from 4 to 3 with no test anywhere in the diff asserting the new value, and no verification that downstream consumers (e.g. the Keycloak Operator, which invokes update-compatibility and branches on its exit code) were updated. Any external consumer coded against the old exit code 4 for 'recreate required' now misclassifies recreate-required results as FEATURE_DISABLED (or an unknown code), silently choosing the wrong upgrade strategy during a rolling deployment. The only test that exercises the recreate path (testWrongVersions) asserts only the error message, never the exit code, so the new mapping 3/4 is entirely unverified.

[ADVISORY] The documentation claims 'Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail' when rolling-updates is not enabled, but the diff contains no operator-side gating code or test verifying that failure mode. Operators following the guide will expect a hard failure when the feature is disabled; if the operator instead proceeds (or fails with an unrelated crash-loop in the pod because the update-compatibility command exits 4), the documented acceptance criterion 'operator fails' is never verified by any test in the diff — UpgradeTest only covers the feature-enabled path.

[ADVISORY] testFeatureNotEnabled only covers the UpdateCompatibilityMetadata subcommand; the identical gate added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() is untested. A regression that removes or bypasses the ROLLING_UPDATES check in UpdateCompatibilityCheck (e.g. reordering before validateConfig) would go unnoticed, leaving the check subcommand usable with the feature disabled while the metadata subcommand is not — sibling gate divergence on the same notification path.

[ADVISORY] The feature-disabled test asserts only the error message and never asserts the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4). The new exit-code contract added to CompatibilityResult (FEATURE_DISABLED = 4) is exercised by no assertion in the diff; scripts and operators that branch on exit code 4 to distinguish 'feature disabled' from 'recreate required' have no regression protection, so a wrong value ships silently.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently changed from 4 to 3, repurposing 4 for FEATURE_DISABLED, which is an unrelated breaking change to an existing public contract not traceable to the stated intent of adding a feature flag. Any existing operator, CI script, or automation keyed on exit code 4 meaning 'recreate upgrade required' now interprets the old value as 'feature disabled' and treats a recreate-required result as a feature-flag error; the new exit-code mapping for 'recreate' is not documented as a change and no migration note is added, so downstream consumers break silently on upgrade.

[BUG] The docs assert the Operator 'will fail' when rolling-updates is not enabled, but the diff contains no operator-side enforcement code — only CLI command guards and test-setup changes are added. The documented invariant is not enforced: an operator user who deploys a Keycloak CR with spec.update.strategy set and no rolling-updates feature enabled gets no failure from the operator; the operator proceeds (or silently produces a non-rolling behavior), so users following the caution box see behavior contradicting the documentation — the actual enforcement only exists in the update-compatibility CLI, not in the operator.

[ADVISORY] The custom test image is rebuilt with --features=rolling-updates unconditionally, changing the runtime configuration for every operator integration test that uses this image, not just rolling-update-specific ones. Operator tests covering unrelated functionality now run with a preview feature enabled, so test results no longer reflect default production configuration; a regression that only manifests with rolling-updates disabled would pass CI while breaking default deployments.

[ADVISORY] The feature-disabled guard runs before validateConfig, so a user with both a misconfigured setup and a disabled feature gets only the feature-disabled message, conflating configuration validation with feature gating in the error surface. Users troubleshooting 'update-compatibility' failures must fix the feature flag before discovering they also have a config error; the two failure modes are reported through the same generic exit path (picocli.exit) with no distinguishing documentation beyond the message, making scripted diagnosis of exit code 4 ambiguous.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently renumbered from 4 to 3 and the value 4 is repurposed to mean FEATURE_DISABLED, breaking every external caller that checks exit code 4 for 'recreate required'. Any CI job, script, or operator-side wrapper that branches on `exit code == 4` to decide 'rolling upgrade not possible' now silently takes the wrong branch: a genuine recreate-required result returns 3 (which those scripts treat as unknown/error or success-adjacent) and code 4 now signals a completely different condition (feature disabled), so existing automation misclassifies outcomes with no error surfaced at the call site.

[BUG] The diff silently repurposes exit code 4 from RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE to FEATURE_DISABLED, changing the meaning of an already-published CLI contract without any consumer migration. Any existing automation or operator release that invokes `kc.sh update-compatibility check` and branches on the documented exit code 4 == 'recreate required' now receives 4 only when the feature flag is off; a genuine recreate-required result now exits 3, which those consumers have never handled, so an in-flight rolling upgrade is treated as success/unknown and proceeds with an incompatible config.

[ADVISORY] The feature-disabled path reports failure only via printError + exit code, while the previously agreed behavior of these preview commands was 'always usable, prints preview warning' — the new hard gate contradicts the command's original intent of assisting every upgrade decision. Operators running the tool during an incident upgrade (feature flag off, e.g. a pre-existing deployment) get a hard failure instead of a compatibility verdict, so they lose the tool's core value exactly when deciding recreate vs rolling; the docs caution is the only notice that the objective changed from 'always advise' to 'advise only when enabled'.

[ADVISORY] The docs caution ('Otherwise, the commands will fail') is the only record of the intent change; the exit-code table row added for outcome 4 documents the new meaning but the guide never states that exit code 3 now means recreate-required, leaving readers of prior versions with stale mappings. Users who scripted against the earlier-documented 4=recreate contract follow a doc table that renumbers semantics without a migration note, producing silent misrouting in their upgrade pipelines.

[BUG] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message and never the exit code, so it cannot distinguish the intended FEATURE_DISABLED (4) exit from a generic usage/software error (1/2). The diff changes the exit-code contract (CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE 4->3, new FEATURE_DISABLED=4), and the operator relies on these codes to choose update strategy; if the command exits with the wrong code (e.g. picocli failing before run() or exit wiring broken), the test still passes and the operator misinterprets the result.

[BUG] The exit-code change from RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE=4 to 3 has no test anywhere in the diff asserting exit code 3 (checked UpdateCommandDistTest — the only exitCode assertion is assertEquals(0, result.exitCode()) in testCompatible, and testWrongVersions asserts only error text, never the exit code). A regression that keeps exiting with the stale code 4 (or any non-3 code) for the recreate case passes the suite, and any external consumer (operator/scripts) keyed on 3-as-recreate breaks silently in production.

[BUG] The new feature-disabled early-return branch in both UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata is exercised by exactly one test (testFeatureNotEnabled) which only checks the stderr string; the return-path wiring (picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED) actually reaching the process exit code) is never asserted, and the metadata command's variant of the message is asserted only via the shared assertError on the same launch of both subcommands in one test. If picocli.exit's value is dropped or the FEATURE_DISABLED constant diverges from what the operator parses, users running `kc.sh update-compatibility` without the flag get an exit code indistinguishable from a hard error, and the test suite reports green.

[BUG] The feature-disabled guard uses Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES) at run() time, but this command writes the server's metadata that is consumed by UpdateCompatibilityCheck on a possibly different installation, and the emitted metadata makes no record of whether the feature was enabled — the doc table (update-compatibility.adoc row 'm|4') presents exit code 4 as 'The feature rolling-updates is disabled', conflating 'feature disabled on the checking server' with 'feature disabled on the server that produced the metadata'. An operator comparing metadata produced by a feature-enabled old server with a check run on a feature-disabled new server (or vice versa) gets exit code 4 with a message about the local flag, masking the actual compatibility verdict; automation that branches on exit codes 0/3 treats 4 as a hard error rather than a recreate decision, and there is no way to distinguish which side was disabled.

[ADVISORY] The doc claims 'the {project_name} Operator will fail' when the feature is not enabled, but this diff contains no operator-side code that validates or enforces the rolling-updates feature before applying an update strategy — the enforcement exists only in the CLI commands (UpdateCompatibilityCheck/UpdateCompatibilityMetadata). A user who follows the docs, sets spec.update.strategy without spec.features.enabled, and relies on the documented operator failure gets undefined behavior: the operator proceeds (or fails with an unrelated error) instead of the documented gated failure, and the docs' promise is unverifiable from the shipped code.

[ADVISORY] The custom image is built with --features=rolling-updates unconditionally, which creates rolling-deploy skew in the upgrade test path this image exists for: the old-version image in an upgrade chain cannot contain this feature, so the very first rolling upgrade from any prior Keycloak version runs with old pods that lack the feature the new operator flow (per the docs' CAUTION) requires. Users attempting the first-ever rolling upgrade into this version hit the bootstrap gap: the feature flag cannot be enabled on the pre-upgrade pods, so the documented hard requirement ('otherwise the Operator will fail') makes the transition rolling-update path impossible or forces a Recreate upgrade for the initial hop — the docs never state this one-version bootstrap restriction.

[ADVISORY] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3 and the new FEATURE_DISABLED takes 4, silently repurposing an existing public exit-code contract for any out-of-tree automation. Existing scripts/CIs that already branch on exit code 4 as 'recreate upgrade required' (the previously documented meaning) will now interpret it as feature-disabled, and code 3 (previously unused/absent in their switch) becomes an unhandled value — the failure is silent because both are non-zero success-like 'verdict' codes, not errors, so nothing crashes; operators get wrong upgrade decisions without any visible failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The docs caution ('Otherwise, the commands will fail') is the only record of the intent change; the exit-code table row added for outcome 4 documents the new meaning but the guide never states that exit code 3 now means recreate-required, leaving readers of prior versions with stale mappings. Users who scripted against the earlier-documented 4=recreate contract follow a doc table that renumbers semantics without a migration note, producing silent misrouting in their upgrade pipelines.

So the guide *does* state the new meaning for exit code 3 via the `m|3` row, and it no longer presents 4 as recreate. Claims about “prior versions”/migration notes and users’ existing scripts cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message and never the exit code, so it cannot distinguish the intended FEATURE_DISABLED (4) exit from a generic usage/software error (1/2). The diff changes the exit-code contract (CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE 4->3, new FEATURE_DISABLED=4), and the operator relies on these codes to choose update strategy; if the command exits with the wrong code (e.g. picocli failing before run() or exit wiring broken), the test still passes and the operator misinterprets the result.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new exit code contract in `CompatibilityResult` (`RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` changed 4→3 and new `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`) and wiring in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck/Metadata.run()` to `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is disabled. In `UpdateCommandDistTest.testFeatureNotEnabled`, the test only asserts the error string and does not assert `cliResult` exit code, so it would still pass if the command exited with a generic picocli error code (1/2) rather than the intended 4. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The exit-code change from RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE=4 to 3 has no test anywhere in the diff asserting exit code 3 (checked UpdateCommandDistTest — the only exitCode assertion is assertEquals(0, result.exitCode()) in testCompatible, and testWrongVersions asserts only error text, never the exit code). A regression that keeps exiting with the stale code 4 (or any non-3 code) for the recreate case passes the suite, and any external consumer (operator/scripts) keyed on 3-as-recreate breaks silently in production.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`, but the updated/added tests in `UpdateCommandDistTest` only assert exit code `0` in `testCompatible` and otherwise assert error text without checking the exit code (e.g., `testWrongVersions`). There is no diff-shown test that would fail if the recreate/"rolling upgrade not possible" path still returned the old code (4) or some other non-3 code. This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage for a behavioral contract change, but it is not itself a verifiable runtime defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new feature-disabled early-return branch in both UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata is exercised by exactly one test (testFeatureNotEnabled) which only checks the stderr string; the return-path wiring (picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED) actually reaching the process exit code) is never asserted, and the metadata command's variant of the message is asserted only via the shared assertError on the same launch of both subcommands in one test. If picocli.exit's value is dropped or the FEATURE_DISABLED constant diverges from what the operator parses, users running `kc.sh update-compatibility` without the flag get an exit code indistinguishable from a hard error, and the test suite reports green.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an early-return branch in both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` that calls `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` after printing `printFeatureDisabled()`. The only new test covering this path is `testFeatureNotEnabled`, which asserts only the stderr message and does not assert the resulting exit code. Also, the test launches both subcommands in one `@Launch({UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME})`, so it doesn’t separately verify each subcommand’s behavior beyond the shared `assertError(...)`. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap for newly added control-flow/exit-code behavior, not a demonstrated functional defect in the implementation itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The feature-disabled guard uses Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES) at run() time, but this command writes the server's metadata that is consumed by UpdateCompatibilityCheck on a possibly different installation, and the emitted metadata makes no record of whether the feature was enabled — the doc table (update-compatibility.adoc row 'm|4') presents exit code 4 as 'The feature rolling-updates is disabled', conflating 'feature disabled on the checking server' with 'feature disabled on the server that produced the metadata'. An operator comparing metadata produced by a feature-enabled old server with a check run on a feature-disabled new server (or vice versa) gets exit code 4 with a message about the local flag, masking the actual compatibility verdict; automation that branches on exit codes 0/3 treats 4 as a hard error rather than a recreate decision, and there is no way to distinguish which side was disabled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows both `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` now short-circuit on the *local* runtime flag `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)` and exit via `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` (exit code 4), after printing "The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled." The generated metadata (`ServerInfo` written by the metadata command) is not shown to record whether rolling-updates was enabled on the producing side, and the docs add a table row `m|4` stating "The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled" without clarifying this is the checking command's local configuration. This is a legitimate UX/semantics/documentation concern introduced by the change, but it is not a verifiable functional defect given the commands intentionally refuse to run when the feature is disabled (as also documented by the new CAUTION blocks).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The doc claims 'the {project_name} Operator will fail' when the feature is not enabled, but this diff contains no operator-side code that validates or enforces the rolling-updates feature before applying an update strategy — the enforcement exists only in the CLI commands (UpdateCompatibilityCheck/UpdateCompatibilityMetadata). A user who follows the docs, sets spec.update.strategy without spec.features.enabled, and relies on the documented operator failure gets undefined behavior: the operator proceeds (or fails with an unrelated error) instead of the documented gated failure, and the docs' promise is unverifiable from the shipped code.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds docs stating the Operator will fail if `rolling-updates` is not enabled (advanced-configuration.adoc), but the only concrete enforcement added in this diff is in the CLI commands `UpdateCompatibilityCheck`/`UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` via `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)` and exiting with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED`. On the operator side, the only change shown is a test (`UpgradeTest`) that now explicitly enables the feature in the CR spec; there is no operator-runtime validation/enforcement code in this diff to make the doc claim verifiable. This is a specific doc/behavior mismatch concern grounded in the shown changes, but not a directly provable runtime defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The custom image is built with --features=rolling-updates unconditionally, which creates rolling-deploy skew in the upgrade test path this image exists for: the old-version image in an upgrade chain cannot contain this feature, so the very first rolling upgrade from any prior Keycloak version runs with old pods that lack the feature the new operator flow (per the docs' CAUTION) requires. Users attempting the first-ever rolling upgrade into this version hit the bootstrap gap: the feature flag cannot be enabled on the pre-upgrade pods, so the documented hard requirement ('otherwise the Operator will fail') makes the transition rolling-update path impossible or forces a Recreate upgrade for the initial hop — the docs never state this one-version bootstrap restriction.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the custom image build now always passes `--features=rolling-updates` (operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image) and docs/CLI now require the preview feature to be enabled. However, the finding’s core claim—an upgrade-chain “old-version image” used in upgrade tests (or user upgrades) cannot include the feature, creating an unavoidable bootstrap gap that makes the first rolling upgrade impossible—depends on upgrade mechanics and image/version coupling that are not shown in this diff. The diff does not demonstrate that this custom image is used as the ‘old-version’ image in an upgrade chain, nor that pre-upgrade pods cannot enable the feature, nor that the Operator will fail in that scenario beyond the documentation text. As written, the finding extrapolates beyond what can be verified from the patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3 and the new FEATURE_DISABLED takes 4, silently repurposing an existing public exit-code contract for any out-of-tree automation. Existing scripts/CIs that already branch on exit code 4 as 'recreate upgrade required' (the previously documented meaning) will now interpret it as feature-disabled, and code 3 (previously unused/absent in their switch) becomes an unhandled value — the failure is silent because both are non-zero success-like 'verdict' codes, not errors, so nothing crashes; operators get wrong upgrade decisions without any visible failure.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (in `quarkus/runtime/.../CompatibilityResult.java`). The CLI commands now `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when the `ROLLING_UPDATES` feature is not enabled. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral contract change for the CLI’s exit codes that could break external automation expecting exit code 4 to mean “recreate upgrade required.” However, the diff does not show it causing incorrect behavior inside the repo itself (tests are updated to pass `--features=rolling-updates`), so it’s better characterized as a compatibility/contract concern rather than a verifiable internal defect.
